decisions.rationale: The frontal master already shows the DJ working both decks; the overhead angle adds no decisive action, so hold the wider performance view in the reference’s restrained style.
Both views show steady mixer work rather than a distinct payoff, and the proposed B stay is long; preserve the clean A master rather than manufacture coverage.
The visible raised-hand response reads best in the frontal A frame at 00:05:20.050; an overhead cut would trade the performer’s energy for less expressive deck detail.
At the phrase boundary, the overhead view usefully isolates the two-handed deck move; take the 10.069 s glance, then return before the detail becomes routine.
The B view exposes a control adjustment, but the A master at 00:05:39.802 keeps the DJ and the action legible; this is not enough contrast to earn another quick switch.
